question:
For the system
$$x+y+z=m$$
$$x-y+z=2$$
$$2x+y-z=1$$

(a) Form the matrix equation and find the inverse of its coefficient matrix.

(b) Use the inverse to express $x$, $y$, and $z$ in terms of $m$.

(c) Determine $m$ if $y=\frac{z}{2}$, and hence obtain the corresponding solution.
explanation:
(a)
The matrix equation is
$$\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\1 & -1 & 1\\2 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}m\\2\\1\end{bmatrix}$$
Let
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\1 & -1 & 1\\2 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}$$
Its determinant is
$$|A|=6\neq0$$
The adjoint is
$$\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 2 & 2\\3 & -3 & 0\\3 & 1 & -2\end{bmatrix}$$
Therefore,
$$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix}0 & 2 & 2\\3 & -3 & 0\\3 & 1 & -2\end{bmatrix}$$

(b)
$$\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix}0 & 2 & 2\\3 & -3 & 0\\3 & 1 & -2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}m\\2\\1\end{bmatrix}$$
$$=\frac{1}{6}\begin{bmatrix}0+4+2\\3m-6\\3m+2-2\end{bmatrix}$$
Thus,
$$x=1,\quad y=\frac{m-2}{2},\quad z=\frac{m}{2}$$

(c)
Given that $y=\frac{z}{2}$,
$$\frac{m-2}{2}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{m}{2}\right)$$
$$\frac{m-2}{2}=\frac{m}{4}$$
$$2m-4=m$$
Therefore,
$$m=4$$
Hence,
$$x=1,\quad y=1,\quad z=2$$
The corresponding solution is $(x,y,z)=(1,1,2)$.

options.C:
(a) $|A|=0$, so the inverse does not exist
(b) The variables cannot be expressed uniquely in terms of $m$
(c) $m=4$ gives infinitely many solutions
